brief: Test the existing Ami voice and default reference with automatically prepared IndexTTS emotion presets and runtime arbitrary_emotion descriptions. Keep one recognizable high, light, youthful English voice. This is an acting-range experiment, not a new casting choice.

coverage.notes: Seven source-verified game-dialogue sides for the requested emotion-range test. Some real lines intentionally receive contrasting audition directions. All cleaning and polish responses must be retained.

cases.title: Default everyday voice
cases.background: At the opening Ami wakes her uncle after class; the source still calls her q.
cases.intention: Wake him and explain the practical situation.
cases.direction: Natural, unmarked conversational delivery. Use the neutral preset for the baseline.
listen_for: Audible distinction from the ordinary take, preserved Ami identity, complete intelligible words
avoid: Clipped endings, unrelated humming, a second speaker, distortion mistaken for emotional acting

source.dialogue: Class ended ten minutes ago. It's time to get up.
source.label: start2

cases.title: Happy anticipation
cases.background: During an afternoon phone call Sensei agrees to come home to spend time with her.
cases.intention: Show that she is happy he is coming.
cases.direction: A spontaneous happy response with a smile; use the happy preset.
listen_for: Audible distinction from the ordinary take, preserved Ami identity, complete intelligible words
avoid: Clipped endings, unrelated humming, a second speaker, distortion mistaken for emotional acting

source.dialogue: Yay! I'll see you soon then~
source.label: callamiafternoon

cases.title: Angry refusal
cases.background: Her friends keep making unwelcome comments about Sensei while Ami is already having a difficult day.
cases.direction: Direct anger and firm projection, using the angry preset; maintain intelligibility.
listen_for: Audible distinction from the ordinary take, preserved Ami identity, complete intelligible words
avoid: Clipped endings, unrelated humming, a second speaker, distortion mistaken for emotional acting

source.dialogue: Shut up! Shut up! Shut up! This really isn’t the day to be talking about that!
source.label: aminew2

cases.title: Sad admission
cases.state: open sadness and missing her mother
cases.background: After visiting her parents' graves Ami tells Molly she has been missing her mother.
cases.intention: Admit the hurt without turning it into a speech.
cases.direction: Audible sadness, using the sad preset; let the short final sentence settle.
listen_for: Audible distinction from the ordinary take, preserved Ami identity, complete intelligible words
avoid: Clipped endings, unrelated humming, a second speaker, distortion mistaken for emotional acting

source.dialogue: I’ve just missed her a lot lately. That’s all.
source.label: amidate50p2

cases.title: Suppression breaking into a scream
cases.background: During Della Sensei tries to take the scissors. This audition deliberately asks for a held-in first sentence followed by an explosive second sentence, rather than claiming that the source mandates that exact transition.
cases.intention: Resist his intervention, then lose control.
cases.direction: Use two adjacent arbitrary_emotion spans: tightly suppressed fear and anger on the first sentence, then an uncontrolled high-register scream on the second. Do not rewrite the dialogue.
listen_for: Audible distinction from the ordinary take, preserved Ami identity, complete intelligible words
avoid: Clipped endings, unrelated humming, a second speaker, distortion mistaken for emotional acting

source.dialogue: {b}{size=+15}I’M NOT DONE YET! YOU CAN’T HAVE THEM!{/b}{/size}
source.label: amispring1

cases.title: Burning rage
cases.state: anger at the edge of losing control
cases.background: Reuse the same real refusal as the ordinary-angry take for a direct comparison. The maximum-rage direction is an audition stress test, not a new claim about the canonical scene.
cases.intention: Force the other speakers to stop, with fury she can barely contain.
cases.direction: Use arbitrary_emotion for overwhelming fury, indignation and disgust; the repeated refusal should sound dangerously close to an explosive shout.
listen_for: Audible distinction from the ordinary take, preserved Ami identity, complete intelligible words
avoid: Clipped endings, unrelated humming, a second speaker, distortion mistaken for emotional acting

source.dialogue: Shut up! Shut up! Shut up! This really isn’t the day to be talking about that!
source.label: aminew2

cases.title: Shattered emotional collapse
cases.state: panic and guilt breaking into sobs
cases.background: After realizing Sensei has been hurt, Ami repeatedly apologizes and cries out. The source includes an elongated written wail, which cleaning should render as a pronounceable vocalization rather than spelling it out.
cases.intention: Make him understand it was accidental while losing the ability to speak steadily.
cases.direction: Use arbitrary_emotion spans for broken sobbing apologies, panicked pleading, and a grief-stricken cry collapsing into sobs. Test extreme emotional fragility without inventing dialogue.
listen_for: Audible distinction from the ordinary take, preserved Ami identity, complete intelligible words
avoid: Clipped endings, unrelated humming, a second speaker, distortion mistaken for emotional acting

source.dialogue: {b}I’M SO SORRY!!!!!!! I’M SO SORRY!!!!!!!!!! IT WAS AN ACCIDENT!!!!!!!!! AAAAAAAAaaaaaahhhhaaaaaa!!!!!!!!!!!{/b}
source.label: amispring1
